purpose: Illustrated Ink replay segmentation and image prompt controls for a Matriarch Tree recall audience in Shale-Root Gallery.

visual_scene_plan.purpose: Click-through visual anchors for the root-gallery locality, ordinary archive labor, multispecies witness staging, embodied ancestral recall, contamination pressure, final priorities, and four state-gated aftermath families.
visual_scene_plan.segmentation_rule: Use separate visual_scene_id anchors for the establishing gallery, Airawa body-and-work introduction, arriving witnesses, preparation choice, prepared ritual fold, embodied recall, cadence mismatch, contamination response, final threshold, and each ending family. The impossible remembered footfall stands alone at the end of the embodied-recall screen before the contamination frame.
visual_scene_plan.prompting_rule: Each base image prompt independently describes camera, gallery geometry, living materials, light, visible body anatomy, interfaces, and props for a general image model. Continuity notes remain tooling constraints; prompt assembly uses concrete visible facts.
visual_scene_plan.global_style_cue: Style: painterly speculative-ecology storybook frame, restrained gouache and ink texture, precise alien anatomy, tactile living infrastructure, cold eclipse blues against amber fungal light and deep root browns, numinous biological wonder, humane workplace detail, readable cinematic composition for illustrated interactive fiction.
visual_scene_plan.prompt_assembly_rule: Assemble each image prompt from the global_style_cue, the scene base_image_prompt, visual refs only for characters or groups listed as visible in that scene, and triggered state_image_modifiers or global_branch_image_modifiers. Use the embedded draft scene-set map for camera and staging continuity; use a hand-built blockout before high-consistency multi-angle rendering.

scene_set_guidance.scope_reason: The fixture remains in one wedge-shaped root gallery but uses several angles, branch-visible object custody, a moving threadwing, and aperture state changes. The embedded map controls draft replay staging.
scene_set_guidance.future_scene_set_need: For website-quality multi-angle generation, build a plan view or simple 3D blockout of Shale-Root Gallery with the outer ledge, uphill crack sightline, four root cups, central work shelf, load-root braces, shallow archive aperture, fungal quarantine lane, salt perch, lantern knots, and entrance path.

scenes.base_image_prompt: Wide establishing view into a wedge-shaped chamber grown between immense dark-brown tree roots and a split wall of black shale on an alien hillside. The chamber opens onto an outer stone ledge at left, where an enormous dark planet hangs fixed in a violet sky and begins to cover a dim red-orange sun. Cold blue bioluminescent knots hang beneath small lantern-tree branches over the ledge. A lane of amber beadlike fungal fruiting bodies enters along the floor. At the deep right wall, four shallow root cups and a translucent veined archive membrane surround a closed oval aperture. Chest-height shelves of grown wood hold carved plate tokens, a mineral bowl, a silver ribbonlike vane, and a damp fungal strand.

visible_characters.default_stance: present through load roots, root cups, and closed translucent aperture
amber fungal bead lane entering from the ledge and ending near the work shelf
cold blue light knots above the outer ledge

visual_continuity_notes: The local coordinate frame is deep/archive-wall at right, outer ledge and exit at left, uphill crack visible beyond the ledge, fungal lane along the lower floor, and lantern knots overhead outside.
The deep organs remain beyond the archive wall. Only the shallow oval aperture and translucent surface membrane enter the playable chamber.

global_branch_image_modifiers.modifier_prompt: Amber sugar-and-mineral mash fills the four root cups; the shallow aperture looks broader and warmer; one rank of blue lantern knots outside is dark.
A silver shed vane is knotted through a carved plate token; the threadwing perches beside it over scattered salt crystals; one blue departure light is allocated outside.
A small ochre scale rests in the witness cup, and faint light connects the archive tender's exposed wrist seam to the shallow membrane.
Three fungal beads close around the damp strand; one bead shows a bitter red core; a gap appears in the blue route-light chain outside.
Both of the archive tender's small lower hands press the pale membrane; identical white pulses and uneven amber pulses compete through her glowing wrist and leg seams.
The silver-vane threadwing makes a tight circuit over the aperture and strikes the suspect fungal strand with a targeted dark dropping before landing at a distance.
The archive tender holds the damp strand with both small lower hands inside a crisp bitter red fungal custody ring separated from the pale aperture.
The archive tender withdraws her carved token and lowers both upper arms; the pale aperture seals while a shallow root presses directionally against her ankle toward the uphill exit.

The opened membrane carries irregular interwoven amber, silver, blue, and body-seam rhythms; the complete historical collapse shows the lower bridge failing on the third uneven pulse; the route witness leaves uphill with clear bodily route posture.

The shallow membrane is torn and clamped shut; identical white cadence lines contaminate both upper and lower route imagery; every root cup is empty and the route witness signals evacuation toward both exits.
Three uneven amber pulses repeat coherently through the load root, fungal beads, the route witness's claw count, and one banking threadwing; bodies beyond the ledge move uphill before stone falls.
The fungal road beads remain closed, blue lantern knots light both exits, threadwing vanes point in conflicting directions, and the route witness carries an Airawa-only warning into divided traffic.
A thick shallow root rises to block the lower exit while blue lantern knots illuminate only the uphill path; the route witness and threadwing move along that tree-selected lane.
The archive wall seals into smooth pale tissue, every directional root withdraws, both blue-lit exits remain ambiguous, and falling dust reaches the outer load root where the two Airawa wait.

Uneven amber pulses travel cleanly through the archive tender's leg seams toward the safe uphill step; the route witness mirrors the movement at one-body distance while the bitter ring remains closed behind them.

The archive tender's left foot reaches toward open air while identical white and uneven amber pulses conflict across her leg seams; the route witness catches her with both large upper arms as amber-red fungal beads form a quarantine ring around both bodies.

visual_character_refs.purpose: Stable character and ecological-body visual identities for prompt assembly. Include only refs for agents or groups visible in a scene.

characters.archive_tender: Archive tender: adult Airawa with a long digitigrade six-limbed body, tiny soft ochre scales, wedge-shaped head, minimal slitlike nose and ear openings, grown brown plate sections with faint amber bioluminescent seams, two large clawed upper arms for load and anchoring, two smaller lower arms with four blunt digits arranged as two opposing pairs for precise work, and grasping feet with four opposing toes and hooked climbing talons. Wears a braided root-fiber waist harness carrying carved plate tokens and shallow mineral cups. Continuity anchors: ochre scales, brown plates, amber seams, root-fiber harness, precise lower-hand work posture.
characters.route_witness: Route witness: adult Airawa with a long digitigrade six-limbed body, tiny charcoal-green scales, wedge-shaped head, grown dark plates with cool gray-green bioluminescent seams, two large clawed upper arms, two small four-digit lower hands, and grasping taloned feet. Fresh gray shale dust sits in plate seams; a narrow blue contract binding crosses the chest. Continuity anchors: charcoal-green body, dusty dark plates, blue binding, fatigued folded posture.
characters.threadwing_witness: Threadwing witness: small flying alien courier with a narrow dark body, tapered head, two gripping feet, and many long silver ribbonlike sensory vanes that read air pressure, chemicals, static charge, heat, and memory residue. Its motion is quick circling, refusal to land, vane flaring, targeted dropping, and precise perching. Continuity anchors: silver sensory ribbons, narrow dark body, salt-cup perch.
characters.shale_root_matriarch: Shale-Root Matriarch visible body: immense dark-brown living roots fused through black shale; a shallow oval archive aperture made of translucent veined tissue; four contracting root cups; thick load roots with old landslide scars; slow signals expressed through tissue color, root pressure, aperture width, and filament reach. Continuity anchors: deep wall at gallery right, four root cups, scarred load roots, translucent oval aperture.

groups.candle_road_delegate: Candle-road delegate: a lane of braided underground fungus visible as thumb-sized amber fruiting beads, damp mineral threads, and a movable dark witness strand. It communicates by bead spacing, amber brightness, bitter red quarantine rings, and narrow opening or closing paths. Continuity anchors: floor lane from outer ledge to center shelf, amber service light, red quarantine state.
groups.lantern_grove: Lantern-grove route organ: small dark-barked branches outside the gallery carrying fist-sized cold blue bioluminescent knots beneath their canopy. The knots trace ledge paths and change through lit gaps, color pulses, or total darkness. Continuity anchors: overhead outer-ledge position, cold blue knots, huge fixed Umbros behind them.
